arith.source:
; Program A (book Laboratory 1, exit criterion): ((7+5)*3) == 36 -> BOOL(true)
        PUSH_S15 7
        PUSH_S15 5
        ADD
        PUSH_S15 3
        MUL
        PUSH_S15 36
        EQ
        EMIT
        HALT

sq.source:
; Subroutine demo: sq(3) + sq(4) = 9 + 16 = 25 -> EMIT -> T0:00000019
        PUSH_S15 3
        CALL sq
        PUSH_S15 4
        CALL sq
        ADD
        EMIT
        HALT

sq:                       ; ( x -- x*x )
        DUP
        MUL
        RET

countdown.source:
; CALL/RET inside a loop: the subroutine consumes and emits the counter copy.
; Emits 5 4 3 2 1 then BOOL(true).
        PUSH_S15 5
loop:
        DUP
        CALL show          ; ( x -- ) emits x
        PUSH_S15 1
        SUB                ; [x-1]
        DUP
        PUSH_S15 0
        EQ                 ; BOOL(x-1 == 0)
        JZ loop            ; nonzero -> keep looping (JZ jumps on false)
        DROP               ; the zero counter
        PUSH_TRUE
        EMIT
        HALT

show:                      ; ( x -- ) emit and drop
        EMIT
        RET

typefault.source:
; Program B (book exit criterion): BOOL(true) + INT(4) -> precise TYPE_FAULT
; at the ADD: pc and stack unchanged, no output.
        PUSH_TRUE
        PUSH_S15 4
        ADD
        HALT

fib.source:
; Recursive fibonacci with CALL/RET (book Lab 1 extension).
; fib(n) consumes its argument and leaves exactly one result:
;   fib(n) = n              if n < 2
;          = fib(n-2)+fib(n-1)  otherwise
; The recursive case keeps n alive across both calls:
;   [n] -> [n, n-2] -> CALL -> [n, fib(n-2)] -> SWAP -> [fib(n-2), n]
;      -> [fib(n-2), n-1] -> CALL -> [fib(n-2), fib(n-1)] -> ADD
; fib(10) = 55 -> EMIT -> T0:00000037
        PUSH_S15 10
        CALL fib
        EMIT
        HALT

fib:
        DUP
        PUSH_S15 2
        LT                  ; BOOL(n < 2)
        JZ fib_rec          ; n >= 2 -> recursive case
        RET                 ; base case: n is the result

fib_rec:
        DUP
        PUSH_S15 2
        SUB                 ; [n, n-2]
        CALL fib            ; [n, fib(n-2)]
        SWAP                ; [fib(n-2), n]
        PUSH_S15 1
        SUB                 ; [fib(n-2), n-1]
        CALL fib            ; [fib(n-2), fib(n-1)]
        ADD                 ; [fib(n-1) + fib(n-2)]
        RET
